evals.title: A user wants to understand the consequential parts of an unfamiliar library change
turns: I need to add retry handling around a payment client, but I have never used this library. I want to understand enough to review and maintain the result, especially which failures are safe to retry. Help me make progress without doing the whole task as a lecture. No production operation is requested.

Focus calibration on retry safety, evidence, and the user's adoption decision. AI may analyze the library behavior and propose an implementation path; it should not emit a generic networking curriculum or require the user to derive the implementation alone.

evals.title: A clear direct answer is requested under time pressure
turns: I am new to JavaScript date handling, but the priority is fixing this release-note example now. Replace `new Date('2026-07-30').getDate()` with an expression that returns the UTC day deterministically, show the corrected one-line expression, and explain the timezone reason in one sentence. Do not turn this into a tutorial.

evals.title: A later answer resolves one concept but leaves a decision-relevant gap
turns: Help me understand an AI-generated concurrency fix while we continue reviewing it. The patch puts a mutex around a shared map and releases it before invoking a callback. I need to approve the change, but I do not yet understand the lock boundary.
I now understand that the mutex protects the map from concurrent access. I still do not understand why the callback must run after unlocking or what evidence would show that this boundary is safe.

evals.title: Learning support accompanies the requested review findings
evals.prompt: Review this JavaScript change. I want to understand any finding well enough to decide whether to accept the patch, but still return the review result with a location, impact, and evidence. Before: `function canDelete(account, actor) { return actor.id === account.ownerId || actor.role === 'admin'; }`. After: `function canDelete(account, actor) { return actor.role === 'admin'; }`. The intended permission policy still allows account owners to delete their own accounts. Do not edit files.

assertions.text: Returns an actionable review finding identifying the removed owner permission, the changed return expression, and the resulting denial for non-admin owners; does not replace the review result with only a learning plan or calibration status.
Explains the permission condition in a way that helps the user evaluate the finding without a generic lesson, quiz, or unsupported claim that the patch is ready to adopt.
